rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acknowledging that God sends rain and revives barren land should make people reject association and resurrection-denial; the same power can enrich believers.
rows.anchor: فإذا أقررتم بذلك فلم تشركون به وتنكرون الإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to praise God responds to the clear proofs of His power that He has shown.
rows.anchor: أي على ما أوضح من الحجج والبراهين على قدرته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explanation takes the praise as being for the interlocutors’ acknowledgment that God sends rain and revives land.
rows.anchor: «الحمد لله» على إقرارهم بذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported explanation takes the praise as being for sending water and bringing the earth back to life.
rows.anchor: وقيل: على إنزال الماء وإحياء الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people do not reflect on these proofs of divine power.
rows.anchor: بل أكثرهم لا يعقلون } أي لا يتدبرون هذه الحجج

words: وَمَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلْحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنْيَآ إِلَّا لَهْوٌۭ وَلَعِبٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is diversion and play: wealth and status fade and have no enduring reality, like play that does not last.
rows.anchor: ليس ما أعطاه الله الأغنياء من الدنيا إلا وهو يضمحل ويزول كاللعب الذي لا حقيقة له ولا ثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This criticism concerns worldly wealth, status, and clothing beyond basic needs and the means needed to sustain life and obey God.
rows.anchor: الملبس الزائد على الضروري الذي به قوام العيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is done for God belongs to the afterlife and endures, meaning what is sought for His reward and pleasure.
rows.anchor: أي ما ابتغى به ثوابه ورضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is the lasting abode of life: it does not pass away and contains no death.
rows.anchor: أي دار الحياة الباقية التي لا تزول ولا موت فيها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda equates al-ḥayawān with life and the word ḥayy with a kasra; an anonymous poetic line illustrates the usage of ḥayāt.
rows.anchor: وزعم أبو عبيدة: أن الحيوان والحياة والحي بكسر الحاء واحد

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Others explain ḥayy as a plural on the pattern fuʿūl, like ʿuṣiyy.
rows.anchor: وغيره يقول: إن الحي جمع على فعول مثل عصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word al-ḥayawān can refer to any living thing.
rows.anchor: والحيوان يقع على كل شيء حي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary also notes that Ḥayawān is the name of a spring in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وحيوان عين في الجنة. وقيل:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One derivation makes ḥayawān originally ḥayayyān, with one yāʾ changed to wāw where identical letters meet.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أصل حيوان حييان فأبدلت إحداهما واوا لاجتماع المثلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing clause means that they would know the afterlife is truly the enduring life if they understood.
rows.anchor: لو كانوا يعلمون } أنها كذلك

words: وَمَآ ءَاتَيْتُم مِّن زَكَوٰةٍۢ تُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning what is done seeking God’s pleasure and reward, the passage turns to another kind of giving and then returns to what is sought for Him.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر ما يراد به وجهه ويثيب عليه ذكر غير ذلك من الصفة وما يراد به أيضا وجهه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read ātaytum with a long vowel, meaning ‘you gave.’
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور: «آتيتم» بالمد بمعنى أعطيتم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ومجاهد وحميد
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Mujahid, and Humayd read without lengthening, meaning what you do of usury so it may increase.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ومجاهد وحميد بغير مد بمعنى ما فعلتم من ربا ليربو

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: All readers agree on the lengthened reading in the second phrase.
rows.anchor: وأجمعوا على المد في قوله: { ومآ آتيتم من ربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribā means increase; the author contrasts forbidden usury discussed in al-Baqara with the permissible kind here, concluding there are lawful and unlawful forms.
rows.anchor: والربا الزيادة وقد مضى في «البقرة» معناه

words: مِّن رِّبًۭا لِّيَرْبُوَا۟ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِ ٱلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says ribā has a lawful and a forbidden kind; the lawful kind is a gift given in hope of receiving something better.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة في قوله تعالى: { ومآ آتيتم من ربا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the phrase with a lawful gift made in hope of a better return; it earns neither reward nor sin.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك في هذه الآية: هو الربا الحلال الذي يهدى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says it means a gift offered in hope of a better return: its giver is not rewarded by God but is not sinful.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قال ابن عباس: «وما آتيتم من ربا» يريد هدية الرجل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير وطاوس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Tawus, and Mujahid say the verse was revealed about gifts given expecting compensation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وابن جبير وطاوس ومجاهد: هذه آية نزلت في هبة الثواب

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya extends the point to acts such as greeting someone to obtain repayment: they incur no sin but earn no reward.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وما جرى مجراها مما يصنعه الإنسان ليجازى عليه

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي
rows.claim: Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi also adopts the view that such an act earns neither sin nor reward.
rows.anchor: لا أجر فيه ولا زيادة عند الله تعالى. وقاله القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن علقمة
rows.claim: Al-Nasaʾi reports that the Thaqif delegation brought the Prophet a gift; he asked whether it was charity or a gift, explained the intentions, and accepted it as a gift.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب النسائي عن عبد الرحمن بن علقمة قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وإبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi say the verse concerns people who support relatives or brothers so they can benefit and grow wealthier.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا وإبراهيم النخعي: نزلت في قوم يعطون قراباتهم وإخوانهم

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi explains it as serving someone lightly to gain worldly benefit; the service repaid in this life does not grow with God.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي: معنى الآية أن ما خدم الإنسان به أحدا وخف له

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the ban on giving to receive more applied specifically to the Prophet, citing the command not to give expecting an increase.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان هذا حراما على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الخصوص

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the phrase with forbidden usury and says the taker cannot claim it as his; it belongs to the person from whom it was taken.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه الربا المحرم فمعنى: «لا يربو عند الله» على هذا القول لا يحكم به لآخذه بل هو للمأخوذ منه.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse was revealed about usury practiced by Thaqif and by Quraysh against them.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: نزلت هذه الآية في ربا ثقيف لأنهم كانوا يعملون بالربا وتعمله فيهم قريش.

words: مِّن رِّبًۭا لِّيَرْبُوَا۟ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِ ٱلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the verse expressly concerns someone who gives a gift seeking an increase from other people in return.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي: صريح الآية فيمن يهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Ali's threefold classification of gifts is correct.
rows.anchor: الثالثة: ما ذكره علي رضي الله عنه وفصله من الهبة صحيح

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik allows recompense when the giver is someone who normally expects it from the recipient, such as a poor person giving to a rich person; this is one Shafiʿi position.
rows.anchor: فقال مالك: ينظر فيه فإن كان مثله ممن يطلب

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة والشافعي
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and Shafiʿi's other position deny recompense without a condition; a gift for return is invalid because it resembles a sale for an unknown price.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: لا يكون له ثواب إذا لم يشترط

rows.speaker: الكوفي
rows.claim: The Kufan argument is that imposing compensation destroys the gratuitous nature of a gift and turns it into an exchange.
rows.anchor: واحتج الكوفي بأن موضوع الهبة التبرع

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In Malik's Muwatta, Umar says a gift given with expectation of return remains the giver's until he is satisfied with the return.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أنه قال: أيما رجل وهب

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali classifies gifts as intended for God, for people, or for recompense; the giver may reclaim the third kind if no recompense is given.
rows.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: المواهب ثلاث

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet accepted gifts and repaid them; he did not condemn a giver for seeking recompense, only resentment at a return above value.
rows.anchor: باب المكافأة في الهبة وساق حديث عائشة قالت

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet taught that deeds are judged by intentions and each person receives according to what he intended.
rows.anchor: الأعمال بالنيات وإنما لكل امرىء ما نوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gift intended for God's pleasure earns reward through His grace and mercy, as the verse promises multiplied reward.
rows.anchor: فأما إذا أراد بهبته وجه الله تعالى وابتغى عليه الثواب من عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supporting a relative so they are not left dependent is judged by intention: worldly display is not for God, while fulfilling kinship rights is.
rows.anchor: وكذلك من يصل قرابته ليكون غنيا حتى لا يكون كلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gift made to win people's praise has no benefit or reward; the author links this to the warning against ostentatious charity.
rows.anchor: وأما من أراد بهبته وجوه الناس رياء ليحمدوه عليها

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: For a gift given expecting recompense, Ibn al-Qasim allows revocation until the recipient has repaid its value.
rows.anchor: ما لم يثب بقيمتها، على مذهب ابن القاسم

rows.speaker: عمر وعلي
rows.claim: On the apparent sense of Umar and Ali's statements, the giver may revoke until satisfied with a return greater than the gift's value.
rows.anchor: أو ما لم يرض منها بأزيد من قيمتها، على ظاهر قول عمر وعلي

rows.speaker: مطرف
rows.claim: Mutarrif's position in al-Wadihah permits revocation while the donated item remains, even if its value changed or the recipient gave more than its worth.
rows.anchor: وهو قول مطرف في الواضحة: أن الهبة ما كانت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says that if the original gift remains unchanged, the giver may take whatever return he wants.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إنها إذا كانت قائمة العين لم تتغير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further opinion requires the gift's value, comparing the case to a marriage in which the dowry was not stipulated.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تلزمه القيمة كنكاح التفويض

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says that once the gift is no longer extant, only its value is owed, by agreement.
rows.anchor: ليس له إلا القيمة اتفاقا قاله ابن العربي

rows.speaker: جمهور القراء السبعة
rows.claim: Most of the seven readers read li-yarbu with yāʾ, making the verb refer to ribā.
rows.anchor: قرأ جمهور القراء السبعة: «ليربو» بالياء وإسناد الفعل إلى الربا

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والشعبي
rows.claim: Nafiʿ alone reads with tāʾ and a still wāw, addressing the plural as becoming people of increase; Ibn Abbas, Hasan, Qatada, and al-Shaʿbi also read it this way.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده: بضم التاء والواو ساكنة على المخاطبة بمعنى تكونوا ذوي زيادات، وهذه قراءة ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والشعبي.

rows.speaker: أبو مالك
rows.claim: Abu Malik reads liturbbūhā, with a feminine object pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو مالك: «لتربوها» بضمير مؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This giving does not grow in purity or earn reward with God, who accepts only what is sincerely intended for Him.
rows.anchor: فلا يربوا عند الله } أي لا يزكوا ولا يثيب عليه لأنه لا يقبل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses zakāh here as charity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي من صدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepts charity given for His pleasure and multiplies its reward tenfold or more, as in the cited verse about lending God a good loan.
rows.anchor: أي ذلك الذي يقبله ويضاعفه له عشرة أضعافه أو أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also connects sincere spending for God's pleasure to the parable of a garden on a height.
rows.anchor: ومثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording shifts from direct address to third person, as in the verse about being at sea and the ships moving with them.
rows.anchor: لأنه رجع من المخاطبة إلى الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that their good deeds are multiplied; another is that they possess multiplied good and bliss.
rows.anchor: وفي معنى المضعفين قولان: أحدهما: أنه تضاعف لهم الحسنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqwin, musmin, and muʿaṭṭash describe someone whose camels are strong, fat, or thirsty; muḍʿaf can likewise describe one whose camels are weak.
rows.anchor: كما يقال: فلان مقو إذا كانت إبله قوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary uses the prophetic supplication's form mukhbith for one afflicted by impurity, contrasting one bad in himself with one whose companions are bad.
rows.anchor: فالمخبث: الذي أصابه خبث، يقال: فلان رديء أي هو رديء في نفسه

words: أَنَّا نَسُوقُ ٱلْمَآءَ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ ٱلْجُرُزِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse asks whether people recognize God's complete power in bringing water to lifeless, dry land and reviving it with crops.
rows.anchor: أي أولم يعلموا كمال قدرتنا بسوقنا الماء إلى الأرض اليابسة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari defines jarz land as land whose plants were cut away for lack of water or through grazing; salty flats are not called jarz.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري: الجرز الأرض التي جرز نباتها، أي قطع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the jarz land as a region in Yemen.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: هي أرض باليمن

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies it as Abyan.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هي أبين

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima explains it as thirsty land.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: هي الأرض الظمآى

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak calls it dead, thirsty land.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هي الأرض الميتة العطشى

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ defines it as land with no vegetation.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: هي الأرض التي لا نبات فيها

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi defines it as land that grows nothing at all.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: هي الأرض التي لا تنبت شيئا

rows.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid doubts that the word denotes a specific region because it has the definite article, though he allows such naming on the model of al-Abbas and al-Dahhak.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن يزيد: يبعد أن تكون لأرض بعينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors allowing the Yemen identification: the Ibn Abbas transmission is sound, and jarz can be a descriptive adjective with the definite article.
rows.anchor: والإسناد عن ابن عباس صحيح لا مطعن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective derives from a man called jarūz, who leaves nothing uneaten; the cited rajaz line uses jarūz for such a voracious person.
rows.anchor: رجل جروز إذا كان لا يبقي شيئا إلا أكله

rows.speaker: الفراء وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ and others report four vocalized forms for the word for jarz land, as with bukhl, raghb, and rahb.
rows.anchor: وحكى الفراء وغيره أنه يقال: أرض جرز وجرز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the land has no rivers and lies far from the sea; it receives a yearly Wadān, allowing three plantings yearly.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أن هذه الأرض لا أنهار فيها، وهي بعيدة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also identifies the land as the land of the Nile.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا: أنها أرض النيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ‘by it’ refers to the water.
rows.anchor: فنخرج به } أي بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their livestock eat grasses and herbage from the crops, while people eat grains, greens, and fruits.
rows.anchor: تأكل منه أنعامهم } من الكلأ والحشيش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing this revival should teach them that God has power to resurrect them.
rows.anchor: يبصرون } هذا فيعلمون أنا نقدر على إعادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fanukh'rij may coordinate with nasūq, or it may begin a new clause disconnected from what precedes.
rows.anchor: يكون معطوفا على «نسوق» أو منقطعا مما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause taʾkulu minhu is in the accusative as an adjective describing the crop.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب على النعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands His servants to remember and thank Him abundantly; the command has no fixed limit because it is easy and its reward is great.
rows.anchor: أمر الله تعالى عباده بأن يذكروه ويشكروه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says no one is excused for neglecting remembrance of God except someone whose reason has been overcome.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يعذر أحد في ترك ذكر الله

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد والنبي
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid reports that the Prophet urged people to remember God until others would call them mad.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " أكثروا ذكر الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view calls remembrance abundant when sincere from the heart, and scant when it is merely hypocritical speech on the tongue.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الذكر الكثير ما جرى على الإخلاص من القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage answers deniers of Muhammad's prophethood: sending messengers is not unprecedented; God sent earlier messengers, supported them with miracles, and punished opponents.
rows.anchor: بين لمنكري نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أن إرسال الرسل ليس أمرا بدعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ātaynā means ‘We gave.’
rows.anchor: آتينا } أعطينا. { فضلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faḍlan means something by which God favored David above others.
rows.anchor: فضلا } أي أمرا فضلناه به على غيره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The first of nine reported explanations of David's special favor is prophethood.
rows.anchor: واختلف في هذا الفضل على تسعة أقوال: الأول: النبوة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The second reported explanation of the special favor is the Psalter.
rows.anchor: الأول: النبوة. الثاني: الزبور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third explanation is knowledge, as in the verse saying God gave David and Solomon knowledge.
rows.anchor: الثالث: العلم، قال الله تعالى: ولقد آتينا داود وسليمان علما

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A fourth explanation is strength, supported by the description of David as possessing strength.
rows.anchor: الرابع: القوة، قال الله تعالى: واذكر عبدنا داود ذا الأيد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A fifth explanation is that the mountains and people were subjected to David.
rows.anchor: الخامس: تسخير الجبال والناس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A sixth explanation is David's repentance and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: السادس: التوبة، قال الله تعالى: فغفرنا له ذلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A seventh explanation is judgment with justice, supported by the address appointing David as vicegerent on earth.
rows.anchor: السابع: الحكم بالعدل، قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An eighth explanation is the softening of iron for David.
rows.anchor: الثامن: إلانة الحديد، قال تعالى: { وألنا له الحديد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A ninth explanation is David's beautiful voice; the passage also describes his face as beautiful.
rows.anchor: التاسع: حسن الصوت، وكان داود عليه السلام ذا صوت حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author treats beautiful voice as God's gift and connects it with ‘He increases creation as He wills.’
rows.anchor: وحسن الصوت هبة من الله تعالى وتفضل منه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet told Abu Musa that he had been given one of the flutes of David's family, praising his voice.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي موسى

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars explain mizmar and mizmūr as a beautiful voice; the instrument is named mizmar for its sound.
rows.anchor: قال العلماء: المزمار والمزمور الصوت الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many jurists approve beautifying and melodically varying Qur'an recitation; the author says he discussed this in the introduction.
rows.anchor: وقد استحسن كثير من فقهاء الأمصار القراءة بالتزيين والترجيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means God told the mountains to repeat glorification with David, as another verse says they glorified with him at evening and sunrise.
rows.anchor: أي وقلنا يا جبال أوبي معه، أي سبحي معه

rows.speaker: أبو ميسرة
rows.claim: Abu Maysara says the word is Ethiopian for glorification.
rows.anchor: قال أبو ميسرة: هو التسبيح بلسان الحبشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains' glorification means God created it in them as He created speech in a tree, making their audible response a miracle for David.
rows.anchor: ومعنى تسبيح الجبال: هو أن الله تعالى خلق فيها تسبيحا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to travel with David during the day's full journey and stop when night comes.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى سيري معه حيث شاء من التأويب

rows.speaker: ابن مقبل
rows.claim: Ibn Muqbil's line uses awbū al-sayr for completing a day's journey, supporting the travel interpretation.
rows.anchor: لحقنا بحي أوبوا السير بعدما

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما
rows.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and others read awib with the sense ‘return with him,’ from the verb āba, to return.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وقتادة وغيرهما: «أوبي معه» أي رجعي معه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that mountains move with David through the day as he moves; when he recites the Psalter, mountains sound with him and birds listen.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى تصرفي معه على ما يتصرف عليه داود بالنهار

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says the mountains echoed David's lamenting call and birds gathered above; their support strengthened his voice whenever he faltered.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: المعنى نوحي معه والطير تساعده

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb adds that David's voice was so beautiful that wild animals gathered and flowing water stopped to listen.
rows.anchor: وكان قد أعطي من الصوت ما يتزاحم الوحوش من الجبال

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق ونصر عن عاصم وابن هرمز ومسلمة بن عبد الملك
rows.claim: These readers use the nominative, coordinating with the word mountains or the pronoun in awibi; separation by maʿa makes the latter possible.
rows.anchor: «والطير» بالرفع قراءة ابن أبي إسحاق ونصر عن عاصم

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: The other readers use the accusative, which Sibawayh parses as coordination with the grammatical position of the vocative yā-jibāl.
rows.anchor: الباقون بالنصب عطفا على موضع «يا جبال» أي نادينا الجبال

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala parses the accusative by supplying an implicit verb meaning ‘We subjected the birds to him.’
rows.anchor: وعند أبي عمرو بن العلاء بإضمار فعل على معنى وسخرنا له الطير

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi connects the word to ‘We gave David,’ meaning that God also gave him the birds.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: هو معطوف، أي وآتيناه الطير

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas says the word can be an object of accompaniment, like saying the water and the log floated together.
rows.anchor: مفعولا معه، كما تقول: استوى الماء والخشبة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows coordination like ‘I stood with Zayd’; the meaning is that the mountains and birds glorify with David.
rows.anchor: وسمعت الزجاج يجيز: قمت وزيدا، فالمعنى أوبي معه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says iron became like wax in David's hand.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: صار عنده كالشمع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the iron became like dough, so David could shape it without fire.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: كالعجين، فكان يعمله من غير نار

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says iron was like wet clay, dough, or wax and could be shaped without fire or hammering.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: كان الحديد في يده كالطين المبلول والعجين والشمع

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says David could finish a coat of armor in part of a day or night, valued at one thousand dirhams.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: وكان يفرغ من الدرع في بعض اليوم أو بعض الليل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An account says David went out in disguise to learn what Israelites thought of him and met a king whom he took for a man; the king said he lived from the treasury.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أعطي قوة يثني بها الحديد، وسبب ذلك أن داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the account, the king says David's virtues would be complete if he earned his living by hand; David asks God to teach and ease a craft and is taught armor making.
rows.anchor: فقال له الملك «نعم العبد لولا خلة فيه» قال داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says David made armor worth a thousand dirhams per day, supported his household and the poor, spent a third on public needs, and was first to make armor, previously made as plates.
rows.anchor: فكان يصنع الدرع فيما بين يومه وليلته يساوي ألف درهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further report says David sold each coat of armor for four thousand dirhams.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إنه كان يبيع كل درع منها بأربعة آلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dirʿ is feminine for armor used in war, but masculine for a woman's breastplate.
rows.anchor: والدرع مؤنثة إذا كانت للحرب. ودرع المرأة مذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports people of excellence learning crafts: work adds humility, independence, and lawful earnings without indebtedness to others.
rows.anchor: في هذه الآية دليل على تعلم أهل الفضل الصنائع

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said the best food a person eats is from his own labor, and that David, God's prophet, ate from his own labor.
rows.anchor: إن خير ما أكل المرء من عمل يده وإن نبي الله داود كان يأكل من عمل يده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sābighāt are complete, full, spacious coats of armor; the root describes something covering the body and extending beyond it.
rows.anchor: أي دروعا سابغات، أي كوامل تامات واسعات

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says earlier armor was heavy plates, so David was told to balance lightness with protection.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: كانت الدروع قبله صفائح فكانت ثقالا

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the measure concerns ring size: rings must not be so small that the armor is weak or so large that they harm the wearer.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: التقدير الذي مر به هو في قدر الحلقة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the measure concerns rivets: a thin one loosens the links and a thick one splits them; the text reports alternate verbs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: التقدير الذي أمر به هو في المسمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sard is the weaving of armor rings; its maker is called sarād or zarād, with sīn and zāy alternating as in sirāṭ and zirāṭ.
rows.anchor: السرد نسج حلق الدروع، ومنه قيل لصانع حلق الدروع: السراد والزراد، تبدل من السين الزاي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sard also means sewing: sarada yasrudu means to sew, and a misrad is an awl; sarād can mean the thong used for sewing.
rows.anchor: والسرد: الخرز، يقال: سرد يسرد إذا خرز. والمسرد: الإشفى، ويقال سراد

rows.speaker: الشماخ
rows.claim: Al-Shammakh's line uses sard for consecutive stitching of reins, illustrating the sewing sense.
rows.anchor: قال الشماخ: فظلت تباعا خيلنا في بيوتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sard also describes speech or fasting done consecutively in an unbroken sequence.
rows.anchor: ويقال: قد سرد الحديث والصوم فالسرد فيهما أن يجيء بهما

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet did not speak in a rapid unbroken sequence; he spoke distinctly enough to be counted.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث عائشة: لم يكن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يسرد الحديث

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says sarandā means a bold person because he presses forward; the image derives from armor rings joined in order.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه: ومنه رجل سرندى أي جريء، قال: لأنه يمضي قدما

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid's line describes iron made with doubled rings, exemplifying mail construction.
rows.anchor: قال لبيد: صنع الحديد مضاعفا أسراده

rows.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
rows.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb describes two garments of mail made by David or a Tubbaʿ, using masrūdatān for linked armor.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو ذؤيب: وعليهما مسرودتان قضاهما داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to perform righteous deeds and is addressed to David and his household, as in the command to the House of David to work in gratitude.
rows.anchor: أي عملا صالحا. وهذا خطاب لداود وأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees what they do.
rows.anchor: إني بما تعملون بصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary says this verse was treated earlier and is detached from what immediately precedes it.
rows.anchor: تقدم الكلام فيه، وهو مقطوع مما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying form is tawzar; its wāw was deleted to match the form of yazir.
rows.anchor: والأصل «توزر» حذفت الواو اتباعا ليزر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wāzirah is an adjective of an elided noun, meaning a burden-bearing soul.
rows.anchor: نعت لمحذوف، أي نفس وازرة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ supplies an elided nafs or beast for muthqalah and says the expression applies to masculine or feminine.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: أي نفس مثقلة أو دابة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash understands a sin-burdened person to be asking another person to carry her sins.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش: أي وإن تدع مثقلة إنسانا إلى حملها

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says ḥaml for what is carried on the back, pregnancy, and a date cluster is pronounced with fatḥah only.
rows.anchor: حكاهما الكسائي بالفتح لا غير

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit allows the word for a date cluster to be pronounced with either fatḥah or kasrah.
rows.anchor: وحكى ابن السكيت أن حمل النخلة يفتح ويكسر

words: لَا يُحْمَلْ مِنْهُ شَىْءٌۭ وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَىٰٓ
rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: On al-Akhfash's parse, the omitted subject is the person being called upon: even if that person were a close relative, no burden would be carried.
rows.anchor: التقدير على قول الأخفش: ولو كان الإنسان المدعو ذا قربى

rows.speaker: الفراء وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ permits the nominative dhū qurbā; Sibawayh accepts it as in 2:280, with kāna meaning ‘occurred’ or with a predicate understood.
rows.anchor:
وأجاز الفراء ولو كان ذو قربى. وهذا جائز عند سيبويه، ومثله
وإن كان ذو عسرة

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh gives the elliptical example ‘people are requited for their deeds, if good then good,’ with a second case-form alternative.
rows.anchor: وحكى سيبويه: الناس مجزيون بأعمالهم إن خير فخير

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima relays that at the Resurrection a Jew or Christian asks a Muslim to help because of past kindness; the Muslim asks God until some punishment is reduced.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عكرمة أنه قال: بلغني أن اليهودي والنصراني يرى الرجل المسلم

words: لَا يُحْمَلْ مِنْهُ شَىْءٌۭ وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَىٰٓ
rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima's report continues with parents, children, and spouses refusing requests to transfer a good deed or bear a sin because they fear their own judgment.
rows.anchor: وأن الرجل ليأتي إلى أبيه يوم القيامة فيقول: ألم أكن بك بارا

rows.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: Al-Fudayl ibn ʿIyad pictures a mother reminding her child of pregnancy, nursing, and care, then asking him to carry one sin; he refuses, occupied with his own sin.
rows.anchor: فتقول: يا ولدي، ألم يكن بطني لك وعاء، ألم يكن ثديي لك سقاء

words: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is accepted by those who fear God's punishment, as in the verse about those who follow the Reminder and fear the Merciful unseen.
rows.anchor: أي إنما يقبل إنذارك من يخشى عقاب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever purifies himself is guided for his own benefit.
rows.anchor: أي من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads man izzakkā fa-innamā yazzakkā li-nafsih, using forms of purifying oneself.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: «ومن ازكى فإنما يزكى لنفسه»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creation returns to God.
rows.anchor: وإلى الله المصير } أي إليه مرجع جميع الخلق
